headline: Approved January 21, 2026 minutes while discussing ordinance updates, court ruling on buffer zones, and license status reports.
summary: The commission approved its January 21, 2026 minutes and discussed proposed updates to license limits and local approval ordinances. Members reviewed a court decision voiding the ordinance's buffer zone section, heard industry and operations updates, and received a police chief report on DMS Trinity's security plan.
decisions: Approved the January 21, 2026 minutes on a motion by Diana Jeong, seconded by Chief Cronin, all in favor.

1 | P a g e  
 
 
 
  
                          
CANNABIS LICENSING AND ENFORCEMENT COMMISSION 
                                       City Hall, 215 Pleasant Street, Conference Room 105 
                                                               Wednesday, March 4, 2026 at 5 PM 
 
Committee Members in Attendance 
√ Nelson Miller Bldg. Commissioner 
√ Ron Hogan, Chair Finance 
V Glenn Cronin Chief of Police 
√ Diana Jeong Mayor’s Appt. 
√ Deano Summers Council Appt. 
√ Kathleen Manning Hall Clerk non-voting mem. 
 
MINUTES ` 
 
1. Roll Call of Committee members: Meeting was called to order at 5 PM and there was a quorum 
sufficient to conduct business. 
 
2. Approval of January 21, 2026 Minutes: Motion by Diana Jeong to approve minutes; seconded by 
Chief Cronin. All in favor, Motion passes.  
 
3. Recommendations to Malden City Council on updates to Ordinances regarding License Limits 
and Local Approval Process. Ron reported that when establishing the Cannabis ordinance, the 
Council wrote that the CLEC would approve five licenses during the initial licensing period, which 
it did.  Another section of the ordinance caps licenses at 20% of liquor licenses (currently 18). 
The CLEC has requested that the ordinances be updated to remove this conflict. Ron Hogan had 
initially communicated with Councillor Karen Colon Hayes and Councillor Steve Winslow back in 
October of 2025 and asked that the ordinances be clarified. An ordinance change will address 
the language and clarification. The hope is that this matter will appear on the next docket. 
 
4. Industry Updates (Diana Jeong and Deano Summers) The application period for delivery licenses 
for Social Equity applicants has been extended. Quarterly reporting of revenue may not be 
accurate, it is currently trending fairly flat, but there was a boost in revenue during the 
snowstorms. 
 
5. Updates on Existing Operations (Misty Mountain Shop & Eastern Cannabis) and License in 
Process (DMS Trinity) (Nelson Miller) Nelson has had no communication with either Misty 
Mountain or Eastern Cannabis. DMS’s Sign has been approved which must be up for final 
inspection from state. 
 
6. Update on court decision, Benevolent Botanicals and Next Steps (Ron Hogan/Nelson Miller) 
The Court’s decision ruled that the particular section of our ordinance regarding buffer zones is 
void and the Ordinance Committee needs to now determine what replaces that. Because the 
Court removed it there are a lot of blank spots in the ordinance which must now be rewritten. 
             MASSACHUSETTS

 Gary Christenson, Mayor

An appropriate replacement must be adopted. Clarification must be made before Benevolent is 
able to move forward. The Council is committed to working through that and to resolving the 
issues. 
 
• Michael Rosen, Council for Benevolent, was in attendance and asked to be recognized. 
He believes the City’s interpretation is mistaken. The Court struck 12.12.190, and he 
believes Benevolent may now seek permits per the court’s ruling. He believes the 
court’s order instructs Malden to allow Benevolent to move forward with Section 6, get 
a building permit, host a second community meeting, enter a host community 
agreement, and apply to the CCC.  
• Ron believes that Mr. Rosen’s interpretation must be interpreted by Malden’s Legal 
Department and that this meeting is not the venue to interpret the Court’s order. The 
agenda item was solely to update the CLEC on the results of the court case decision. Mr. 
Rosen and his discussion are not on the agenda and as the CLEC was recently the subject 
of an open meeting law violation for allowing someone to speak who was not properly 
on the agenda this conversation cannot be held. Nelson reiterated that a discussion 
needs to be had with our Legal Dept. 
 
7. Regulatory Updates (Ron Hogan) No updates. 
 
8. Police Chief Report (Glenn Cronin) Chief Cronin received an email from the state asking if he 
received DMS’s security plan, and if a walk through has been done. A walk through was done 
five months ago. The Chief will get back to them on the security plan. 
 
9. New Business No new business. 
 
Motion to adjourn by Deano Summers, seconded by Diana Jeong Deano Summers - meeting adjourned.
